document_title: Limited or Sunset? What Alaska Adds to the E-Rate Record
post_copy:
Alaska has about 0.2 percent of the country's people and about 7.3 percent of its funded E-Rate commitments.

That is $195.2 million in USAC funded commitments for funding year 2025. Only California and Texas drew more. Lower Kuskokwim School District alone holds $91.0 million of it, 46.6 percent of Alaska's total.

The FCC asks whether E-Rate should be limited or sunset. It also asks what connectivity schools need to use AI-enabled tools. The full notice never uses the word Alaska. Comments are due October 13th.

The population share against the money share, ten districts ranked by dollars, one district's internet line over four years and a worksheet of FCC questions with one Alaska answer blank.

How should the FCC weigh a state where one district holds 46.6 percent of its E-Rate money?

#ERate #AlaskaSchools #RuralBroadband

aftercare: Post Thursday, October 1st, or Tuesday, October 6th, between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time. Cadence is your call. The window is long, but earlier in it leaves more days for a reader to file.
Paste the sources block as the first comment within 60 seconds of posting.

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. If a reader asks how to file, point to slide 9 (docket 26-133, ECFS). If a reader asks whether the FCC has decided to cut E-Rate, say no: the notice asks questions and the deck takes no side.
Docket deadlines to keep in view: comments are due October 13th and replies November 12th. After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger.
editor_notes_for_email: This deck says Alaska draws $195.2 million in USAC funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025 (third in the nation, 7.3 percent of $2.69 billion, against about 0.2 percent of U.S. residents), that one district (Lower Kuskokwim, $91.0 million) holds 46.6 percent of it, and that the FCC notice asks whether E-Rate should be limited or sunset and what connectivity schools need for AI tools, with comments due October 13th and replies November 12th. It deliberately does not claim that funded commitments are need, that the FCC has decided anything (the notice asks questions and takes no position), or that Alaska is the notice's target. The notice never uses the word Alaska (a full-text search by the showrunner), and the deck says only that. Slide 08 keeps one blank Alaska answer for screen time limits on purpose. The Starlink reason on slide 07 is the Anchorage Daily News's, and only USAC's numbers are printed. The ADN's $96.5 million for Lower Kuskokwim and its $6.25 million and $600,000 for Lower Yukon are not printed because they differ from USAC's. Please verify before posting: (1) USAC data is live, so re-run the C16 and C24 links and confirm $195.2 million and $91.0 million still hold; (2) the Census figures were read through a reader rendering because census.gov returned 403 (confidence 0.85), so confirm 737,270 and 341,784,857 at the QuickFacts link; (3) the six pins on slide 4 mark district office towns, not boundaries, and three of those town claims rest on a reader rendering of the district sites; (4) FY2026 is a part year and is never shown as a decline.
